propositions: The complexity lock compares branch baselines against main tip instead of merge base, causing it to flag ceiling reductions made by main as false violations on un-rebased branches
When main lowers a complexity ceiling, all open changes carrying the pre-reduction baseline fail the lock gate with a false 'ceiling RAISED' violation despite making no actual changes
The gate cannot distinguish 'branch raised ceiling' from 'main lowered it underneath un-rebased branch', so every future ceiling reduction on main breaks the fleet identically
The fix compares branch against merge-base(main, HEAD) instead of main tip, reading the baseline at the merge-base commit and applying unchanged lock rules only to entries the branch itself changed
When merge base cannot be computed, the gate falls back to main-tip comparison with explicit notice, preserving fail-closed posture without silently passing genuine raises
